body:
jordan: Quick heads up — CI started failing with 401s on our SDK tests after switching secrets to the new vault. Anyone seen weird Basic auth header errors?

mei: Yep, saw this earlier. Turned out the secret had a trailing CR (carriage return) from copying via Windows Notepad. The Authorization header included the extra bytes so the base64 didn't match.

jordan: Ugh. I inspected the header emitted by our Node middleware: it showed `Authorization: Basic e3Bhc3N9DQo=` — that trailing `DQo=` decodes to a CRLF. The Node auth util wasn't trimming.

sam: For context, our Node client does `Buffer.from(`${key}:`).toString('base64')` — if `key` contains `\r` it's included. The Python SDK had a `.strip()` in the auth helper so it silently worked there.

lina: Repro steps I used: on Windows copy the API key from Notepad, paste into GH Actions secret, then in a workflow run `echo "$KEY" | od -c` shows `\r` at the end. Quick fixes: `echo -n "$KEY"` or `tr -d '\r'` when setting the secret. Example: `gh secret set API_KEY --body "$(echo -n $KEY)"`.

jordan: Also noticed this made streaming connections fail oddly — server accepted first frame then returned 401 on subsequent frames and our retry logic turned into a tight loop. I'm going to add validation to fail fast if the decoded auth looks malformed.

dev-bot: Reminder: please add a unit test to the auth util and bump test coverage for the client before merging.

mei: Minimal Node patch I tested: `key = key.replace(/[\u0000-\u0020]+$/,'')` — strips trailing whitespace incl `\r`/`\n` and NULs. Also added a small sanitized log: `console.debug('auth key len=', key.length)` (never log the key itself).

sam: I'll open a PR with that patch + a test that simulates a `\r`-terminated secret and asserts header correctness. Also adding a GH Actions step that runs `printf '%s' "$KEY" | od -c` as a debug step when flaky.

jordan: :thumbsup: Thanks. I'll add a short note to devex/docs about the Notepad -> GH Secrets gotcha and a snippet to normalize keys in CI:  ```bash
# normalize API key when setting secret from a file on Windows
cat keyfile | tr -d '\r' | gh secret set API_KEY --body -
```

lina: Can we also add a tiny helper in our test harness to assert env secrets have no leading/trailing whitespace? Could save future time.

sam: Good call. I'll include that in the PR checklist and ping reviewers once it's up.

jordan: Cool — moving this to in-progress. If anyone hits the same in the meantime, `echo -n` or `tr -d '\r'` is the quick workaround.
